415.history: The narrow hill was a mining camp worked by night crews in the last decades of the age. Griogair mac Ailein died in the Company's lock-up there, held for a short-weighted cartload he did not cut, and Thomas Hale came to read the surgeon's note over his grave. The day shift stood in the yard in silence for the night crews, the Lamp-Watch's purse ran dry keeping the strikers fed, and the strike was broken by crews brought in through Muileann dhomhain. The lung-rot was worse there than on any other hill. In the hundred and forty-eighth year its overseer threw down his staff in the week Mòrag broke hers. Its crews were among the first to work by the clay lamps of Baile ghorm, and the pithead there was lit all night from the year the night shift began.

152.history: The harbour on the straight headland of the gulf became the Company's second coal port in the seventieth year, to carry off the yield of the southern workings without the long haul round to Ros dhomhain. Edward Vane laid an iron tram-road drawn by mules from the pits down to its quay; it halved the cost of shipping coal and ended the carting trade of the villages on the old road. The Green Death fell on it among the first of the coast towns. It is the harbour of Cnoc mhòr's cattle trade, and the drovers kept their own quay beside the Company's coal stage for the whole of the age.
152.known_for: the tram-road and the second coal stage

246.history: The narrow mill town in the eastern hills held, in the cellar under its mill house, the copies of the custodians' rolls that the three households of the town made fair winter after winter, the fullest record of the eastern hills and the one no stranger's eye was meant to read. Gormshuil nic Fhearchair was called back from it to the council in the first years, and the rubbing of the first mark went to its loft. Seònag Bhàn kept the copying until her eyes failed, and Cailean mac Eachainn took up the hand at four-and-twenty; it was there he found the Line of Aisling and there, in the last days of the hundred and fiftieth year, that the four chests of the age's rolls came down to him by cart. The copying was done at a long table under a single window, and every copy was made twice, so that no one fire or flood could take the only record of a town.

202.history: The mill on the deep race grew rich carrying grain to the camps. When the crews brought to break the strike at Cnoc chaol were marched through it, its townsfolk turned them from every door, and they slept in the Company's barns; several went home the next season. After the Rending of Cill ghlas its custodians met the people of the closed district on the moor road and lent them common ground, on which they built Achadh chaol. It is the seat of its province, and its custodians had long kept the right of the old roads to shelter any traveller who asked; they held that right did not reach men sent to take other men's work.
202.known_for: the doors shut on the strikebreakers

198.history: The black hill of the charcoal burners kept an old customary cutting held by one family since An Aois Naomh. Under Dunstan's rule the working was taken from them because a great-grandmother of the line had married a human sailor, and the rolls of the hill set down that this was the whole of the reason given. It is the largest of the cluster of charcoal hills, and its people burned charcoal for the Company's smithies after the cutting was taken.

3.history: The open market town of the south-eastern farms has no walls. Its potteries took a contract in the years of the night shift for clay lamp-bodies for the night crews, thousands in a year, and the potters' own book notes that they were the first lamps made on the island for work in the dark by command. Its people kept the Old Spirits through the age. Its fairs bring the south-eastern farms' grain and wool, and its potters kept working the same clay for household crocks when the contract ended.
